title: PosSyncRequested v1 payload
description: ADR 0012. A durable PostgreSQL schedule came due, or an operator asked to resume a run that failed before REVIEW_REQUIRED. The consumer starts (or restarts) a catalog import for the named binding. Identifiers only: no provider credential, no menu content, no customer data.

requestId.description: Identifies this one request, not the run it produces -- the run gets its own id when PosCatalogSyncService opens it. Carried so the same claimed schedule occurrence is traceable end to end through the outbox and the inbox.

tenantId.description: Also the envelope tenant. The handler uses the envelope's tenant as verified context and never a value read back out of this field.

bindingId.description: The ADR 0026 binding to synchronize. Also the partition key and the outbox aggregate id, so at most one PosSyncRequested for a binding is ever in flight -- a dead-lettered command blocks a new one for the same binding rather than piling up behind it.

scheduleId.description: The integration.pos_sync_schedules row that claimed this occurrence. Null for an operator-triggered resume, which has no schedule of its own.

resumedRunId.description: Set only when triggerType is RESUMED: the prior run that failed before REVIEW_REQUIRED and could not be picked up mid-fetch (the first provider offers no incremental read to resume with), so this request opens a fresh run that records where it resumed from.

triggerType.description: SCHEDULED: the durable timer decided this was due. RESUMED: an operator asked to retry a run that failed before staging completed a review. A manual dry run never reaches this topic -- it runs synchronously from the control-plane request.

requestedAt.description: When the schedule was claimed or the resume was requested, not when the command is eventually handled.
